## loadViewForPath()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function loadViewForPath(pathName: string): Promise<ComponentType<any>>;
```

Loads the view the given browser path addresses.

**Parameters**

| | |
|---|---|
| `pathName` | location.pathname  |

**Returns** the view component

## loadView()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function loadView(name: string): Promise<ComponentType<any>>;
```

Loads the view with the given name and returns its default export.

The module is only fetched the first time its view is actually requested -- the application registers
loader functions, not modules.

**Parameters**

| | |
|---|---|
| `name` | view name, e.g. "Home" or "sub/View"  |

**Returns** the view component

## routeOf()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function routeOf(pathName: string): string;
```

Converts a browser path name into an application route.

**Parameters**

| | |
|---|---|
| `pathName` | location.pathname  |

**Returns** route without leading or trailing slash, lower case. "" for the application root itself.

## ViewRoute()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function ViewRoute({ route, children }: ViewRouteProps): JSX.Element;
```

Says which route the view below it is, for a view rendered anywhere but at its own URL: on a docs page, in a
Storybook story, in a component test, several views on one page.

A view reads its injections by route -- useInjection(Q_FooList) in app/grid/Sorting.tsx reads
"grid/sorting/Q_FooList" -- and takes the route from the location where nothing says otherwise. startup()
renders a view at its own URL, so an application doesn't need this. FixtureScope provides one from its
fixture.

    <ViewRoute route="grid/sorting">
        <Sorting/>
    </ViewRoute>

## ViewRouteProps

<span class="api-kind">type</span>

```ts
type ViewRouteProps = {
  /**
   * Route of the view below, as routeOf() gives it for the view's own URL: "grid/sorting". Slashes at either end
   * and case don't matter.
   */
  route: string;
  children: ReactNode;
};
```

:::note[Undocumented]
This export carries no doc comment in the source.
:::

## useRoute()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function useRoute(): string;
```

The route of the view the calling component belongs to: the nearest ViewRoute's, otherwise the location's.

Rules of hooks apply.

**Returns** route without leading or trailing slash, lower case

## urlOf()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function urlOf(route: string): string;
```

Returns the URL for the given route, e.g. "sub/view" -> "/app/sub/view" in production.

**Parameters**

| | |
|---|---|
| `route` | route without leading slash |

## appBase()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function appBase(): string;
```

Returns the URL prefix the application is served under, with a trailing slash.

The application's Vite `base` is the single source of truth here, so that the dev server and
ViteIndexController agree on where the application lives and a view has the same route either way. The
servlet context path is prepended because Vite knows nothing about it.

## routeNames()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function routeNames(): string[];
```

Returns all routes that resolve to a view, sorted.

## viewNames()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function viewNames(): string[];
```

Returns the names of all registered views, sorted.

## ViewModules

<span class="api-kind">type</span>

```ts
type ViewModules = Record<string, () => Promise<unknown>>;
```

Map of module path to a function loading that module -- exactly what `import.meta.glob(pattern)` returns
when the `eager` option is not set.
